subject: Re: 🔵{Brand} & MobUpps
body:
Hi RECIPIENT_NAME,
Following up on my note about paying for the retained D7 racer rather than the cheap install. The fresh angle is where the spend goes. UK casual CPI sits at just 1.50 to 3.50 pounds on iOS and 0.80 to 2.00 on Android (admiral.media 2025), so volume buying loads up on players who never see a second session. Top casual titles end the year near 14 to 15 percent D7 against a 15 to 20 percent average (gamebizconsulting 2026). A holdout-tested Mario Kart Tour curve shows real cost per kept player. Worth comparing?
angle: fresh angle: UK casual CPI band cheap vs D7 retention gap, spend decided on the return
register_notes: Stage 2 EN gaming_casual (UK): acknowledges second follow-up and references prior outreach in the first sentence; fresh angle = UK casual CPI band (1.50-3.50 iOS / 0.80-2.00 Android) set against top-title D7 14-15 percent vs 15-20 percent average, framing spend as decided on the return; market context real and web-verified, both numbers carried from the parent's verified sources (admiral.media 2025, gamebizconsulting 2026 in enrichment_sources); rotates to Mario Kart Tour from the parent's brand set; no MobUpps figure this stage; 1 question mark; native UK register; no sign-off; no em-dash; no 'X, not Y'.
